summary.text: A 55-year-old man with untreated HIV and a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction with an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, atrial fibrillation and COPD on home oxygen presented for evaluation of a newly diagnosed plasma cell malignancy after presenting one week earlier to an outside hospital with progressively worsening shortness of breath. CT there showed pneumonia, lytic rib lesions and liver masses, and a liver biopsy showed a plasmacytic infiltrate with Ki-67 above 90%. He was then transferred to the authors' institute.

Workup at the institute included a bone survey and bone marrow biopsy without evidence of lytic lesions or myeloma, and PET-CT with hypermetabolic hepatic masses, lytic skeletal lesions and increased distal rectal uptake. Colonoscopy and endoscopic ultrasound showed a submucosal rectal mass raising suspicion for leiomyoma. FNA showed plasma cells positive for CD138 and EBV ISH, and flow cytometry and FISH led to a diagnosis of plasmablastic lymphoma.

Antiretroviral treatment with emtricitabine, tenofovir and dolutegravir was started, and EBV viremia rose from 26,000 to 381,000 copies by discharge; the infectious disease team determined no treatment was necessary. He received bortezomib-CHOP chemotherapy, with daratumumab, considered because the lymphoma cells were CD38 positive, started with the fourth cycle after an insurance-related delay, and on continual follow-up achieved complete remission about five months after initiation of treatment.

After five months in remission a chest mass relapse was confirmed by biopsy and treated with salvage chemotherapy, without Adriamycin because of an ejection fraction of 20%. PET-CT after the first cycle showed complete resolution, but at the fifth cycle a repeat PET-CT showed relapse at the same site. Given poor functional status, he was not a candidate for further chemotherapy and was transitioned to comfort measures through palliative care.

ambiguities.issue: CD4 cell count is printed as 128 in the abstract but as 124 in the case presentation, once "at admission" and once restated in the hospitalization paragraph without its own time. The one-character difference is treated as a print artefact (ambiguity, not a source conflict); the case-text value 124 at admission is the recorded fact and the untimed restatement is not recorded as a second measurement.

evidence.quote: CD4 (cluster of differentiation 4) cell count of 128
CD4) cell count at admission - 124
His CD4 count was 124.

ambiguities.do_not_infer: Do not choose between 128 and 124 as the true count beyond the case text.

ambiguities.issue: Lytic lesions: the outside CT and the PET-CT describe lytic lesions, while the institute bone survey did not reveal evidence of lytic lesions. These are different modalities and are recorded as separate observations, not as a conflict.

evidence.quote: multiple lytic lesions in the ribs
a bone survey that did not reveal any evidence of lytic lesions

ambiguities.do_not_infer: Do not treat the bone survey as negating the CT or PET-CT findings.

ambiguities.issue: The colonoscopy lesion size (1.5 cm x 1.5 cm) and the endoscopic ultrasound mass size (3.2 cm x 2.7 cm) come from different examinations and are not stated to be the same measurement.

evidence.quote: a submucosal lesion of 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm
measuring 3.2 cm x 2.7 cm

ambiguities.do_not_infer: Do not merge or reconcile the two sizes.

ambiguities.issue: The remission time is anchored to "initiation of treatment" without naming whether this is bortezomib-CHOP or antiretroviral treatment; the two treatments are both described as started, so the anchor is kept literal.

evidence.quote: about five months after initiation of treatment

ambiguities.do_not_infer: Do not attach the remission to a single named regimen.

ambiguities.issue: Liver-biopsy and flow-cytometry markers other than CD38 are not linked to the lymphoma tumor record: the liver masses are never stated to be plasmablastic lymphoma and the flow-cytometry specimen is not named. FNA markers are linked because the abstract identifies the FNA-sampled lesion as plasmablastic lymphoma.

evidence.quote: A liver biopsy was performed revealing a plasmacytic infiltrate
Flow cytometric analysis showed cells positive for CD138

ambiguities.do_not_infer: Do not attribute the liver infiltrate or unspecified flow specimen to the anorectal lymphoma tumor record.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the three images are reviewed in visual.json.

Overall disease status (remission, relapse) is recorded as time-specific outcomes and conditions rather than a single tumor status.
Discussion and conclusion segments are literature or general statements and are not copied to the patient.
The source gives no calendar dates; times are relative and literal.
